issues.current: '1 staff per 16 individuals physically present while individuals sleep' / '1 present overnight'
issues.correct: §6400.45(b) requires one staff per 16 individuals physically present when sleeping. A separate section, §6400.232 'Awake staff persons', says a staff person counted in the §6400.45(b) ratio shall be awake.
issues.evidence: Chapter 6400 text: 'A staff person counted in the ratio as specified in § 6400.45(b) (relating to staffing) shall be awake.'
issues.fix: Add: 'overnight staff counted in the ratio must be awake (§6400.232; confirm applicability to each home type); sleep-shift pay differentials cannot be assumed.' Also add §6400.45(d): the staffing ratio and qualifications in each individual plan must be implemented as written, even above the §6400.45(a)-(c) minimums. The 730 h/home hours figure itself is consistent with the rule.

issues.current: 100% of residents charged $715.68/month for room and board; only the 72% cap and the board-only 32% cap are mentioned
issues.correct: The cap is 72% of (SSI max + PA SSP). It is 72% of total monthly income if income is below the SSI maximum, and $0 if income is below the personal needs allowance. A room-only charge is capped at 40%. Board stops on the 8th consecutive day of leave or hospitalization. Room stops after more than 30 consecutive days hospitalized. Room and board cannot be charged during respite. Form DP 1077 is mandatory.
issues.evidence: Bulletin 00-25-01: 'Form DP 1077 must be used for all Room and Board Agreements.' Increases that reduce personal funds need 30 days' written notice.
issues.fix: Add the 40% room-only cap, the income-below-SSI rule, the leave/hospitalization/respite exclusions, the Form DP 1077 requirement (before admission, annually, 15 days after an emergency placement) and the 30-day increase notice. Apply a vacancy/leave haircut to room-and-board revenue. The $715.68 figure itself (72% x $994) is arithmetically correct and at or below the cap.

issues.current: Opex has no line for incontinence supplies, basic cable, or laundry/lawn/housekeeping labor
issues.correct: Provider-borne room-and-board items include: incontinence products not covered by insurance; a basic cable/streaming package; one landline that works in a power outage (staff cell phones do not count); basic internet; cleaning products; toiletries, towels and bedding; furniture; and all labor for laundry, lawn care, food preparation, maintenance and housekeeping.
issues.evidence: Bulletin 00-25-01 lists these items as part of the provider's room-and-board costs and says provider must 'equip each Home with at least one telephone that will function in the event of a power outage'.
issues.fix: Add per-home lines for a power-outage-capable landline and basic cable, and per-resident lines for incontinence supplies. Budget housekeeping/maintenance labor in staffing. Separately budget paid training time (24 h/yr per direct-care worker plus orientation), because the $350/month training line appears to cover only CPR/first aid and background checks.
